title: Move a story into a theme by drag and drop
prompt:
# Story 3: Move a story folder by drag and drop

- **Story**: XXX-move-story-to-theme
- **Created**: 2026-11-15
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: drag `003-checkout-form` onto `payments`, then onto `reporting`, then back onto `stories`; drag it over its own theme and see no
  highlight; press Escape during a drag; open a link to a story that is in a closed theme.

## Story

As a team member, I want to drag a story folder into the theme I think it belongs to, out of it, or to another theme, so that I decide
myself which stories sit together.

## Acceptance tests

Dragging and dropping

- [ ] **Given** the story folder `003-checkout-form` outside any theme and the theme `checkout-flow`, **When** the user drags the story
  folder onto the theme and drops it, **Then** the story folder is inside the theme and no longer outside, the count of the theme goes up
  by one, the count of `stories` does not change, and the theme opens.
- [ ] **Given** a story folder is being dragged, **Then** a theme it can be dropped on, or the `stories` row, is highlighted while the
  pointer is over it, the theme's row and the rows inside it alike.
- [ ] **Given** a story folder in a theme, **When** the user drops it on the `stories` row, **Then** it goes back outside any theme, in the
  order of its number.
- [ ] **Given** a story folder in theme A, **When** the user drops it on theme B, **Then** it is in B and no longer in A.
- [ ] **Given** a story folder dragged over the theme it is already in, or, outside any theme, over `stories`, **Then** nothing is
  highlighted, and dropping it there changes nothing.
- [ ] **Given** a drag, **When** the story folder is dropped anywhere else, or the user presses Escape, **Then** nothing moves and no
  highlight is left.

What can be dragged

- [ ] **Given** the tree, **Then** only story folders can be dragged: not a theme, not a file, and nothing in `drivers`, `adrs` or
  `architectural-enablers`. A theme cannot be dropped into a theme, so themes never nest.

What a move keeps

- [ ] **Given** a story that is moved, **Then** its identity, text, status, links (both ways), tasks, diagrams and UI example are not
  changed, and if it was open, it stays open with its new path.
- [ ] **Given** a story in a theme, **Then** inside the theme the story folders are in the order of their numbers.
- [ ] **Given** a link that opens a story inside a closed theme, **Then** `stories`, the theme and the story folder open, and the story
  shows selected.
- [ ] **Given** a story in a theme, **Then** the path shown in the builder, and the "File:" line of every prompt about it (edit, diagram, UI
  example), is `stories/<theme>/<identity>/story.md`.
- [ ] **Given** moved stories, **When** the page is reloaded, **Then** each story is in the theme it was moved to.

## Business rules and constraints

- **A story belongs to one theme at most.** Moving it into a theme takes it out of the one it was in.
- **A move is not an edit.** It does not change the text or the status of the story.
- **Dropping where the story already is is not a drop target**, so the tree never offers a move that does nothing.

## Out of scope

- Moving a story with the keyboard or on a touch screen. This story is drag and drop with a mouse or a pen. Whoever builds it should raise
  the keyboard way as its own story (see "Something to decide").
- Moving several stories at once, and reordering stories by hand.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add the theme of a story to the stored story and to its entry, so that its folder path is `stories/<theme>/<identity>`.
- [ ] Make story folder rows draggable, and the theme blocks and the `stories` row drop targets, with the highlight and the cases that do
  nothing.
- [ ] Move the story in the data, and open the theme it lands in.
- [ ] Open the theme of a story when the story is opened from a link.
- [ ] Test a move into a theme, between two themes, back to `stories`, and a drop where the story already is.

tasks.text: Extend the story data model and its store to record the theme a story belongs to, and derive its folder path as `stories/<theme>/<identity>` or `stories/<identity>` accordingly (ADR-0007, Architecture)
Add a drag handle to story folder rows and make them draggable; leave theme rows, files, and all non-story items non-draggable
Make theme rows and the `stories` row into drop targets; highlight a valid target while the pointer is over it; suppress the highlight when the story is already there
Handle the drop: move the story in the store, remove it from its previous theme if any, open the destination theme, and order stories by number
Handle Escape and drops on invalid targets: restore the tree to its pre-drag state with no highlight
Update the path shown in the builder and the "File:" line in prompts to reflect the story's current theme
Open the theme of a story when the story is navigated to via a link, selecting the story
Persist theme membership so that it survives a page reload

Write Jest tests covering: move into a theme, move between two themes, move back to `stories`, drop where the story already is, Escape during drag, and link navigation to a story inside a closed theme (Practice: Pair programming, ADR-0005)
Verify the full build and test suite still completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build)

Add a `PATCH /projects/{projectId}/themes/{themeId}/stories` endpoint (or equivalent) in the inbound adapter that accepts a story identifier and records the move; add a corresponding `PATCH` to remove a story from all themes when it is moved to the `stories` root (ADR-0017, Architecture)
Implement the application-layer command handler that updates the theme aggregate: adds the story identifier to the destination theme's list and removes it from the source theme's list (ADR-0017)
Add or extend the outbound adapter and Flyway migration so that the theme record stores the ordered list of story identifiers that belong to it (ADR-0010, ADR-0011)
Handle the drop: optimistically move the story in the store, call the backend, revert and show an error on failure; on success open the destination theme and order stories by number
On builder load, read theme membership from the backend and populate the store

Write Jest tests covering: move into a theme, move between two themes, move back to `stories`, drop where the story already is, Escape during drag, link navigation to a story inside a closed theme, and backend failure reverting the tree (Practice: Pair programming, ADR-0005)
Write backend unit and integration tests covering the command handler and the persistence of story-identifier lists in themes (ADR-0009, ADR-0012)
